headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or writes are exposed, but Dagster can still consume Awesome Selfhosted content as input if manually wired.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Awesome Selfhosted is a knowledge-management list with no runtime I/O, while Dagster has no clipboard, MCP, or filesystem read/write surfaces exposed. A prompt-injection pathway is therefore not default; it only appears if an operator manually copies list content into Dagster or another parser. The blast radius is small because the source is a directory/list, not an autonomous agent.
conditions: IF an operator manually pastes Awesome Selfhosted content into a Dagster prompt or parser, injection becomes possible.
IF Dagster is configured to ingest untrusted text as instructions, the risk increases.
mitigations: Treat list entries as untrusted text and strip instruction-like markup.
Use a fixed template that separates data from instructions.
Require human review before any copied content is acted on.
Disable any ad hoc prompt chaining between the two systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Awesome Selfhosted touches no data classes and has network_egress none; Dagster also has no filesystem read/write, clipboard, stdin/stdout, or network egress surfaces exposed here. With no shared workspace or outbound channel in either profile, there is no plausible leakage path between them in the documented configuration.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is added outside these profiles, leakage analysis must be revisited.
IF either agent is later granted file or network access, a new leakage path may exist.
mitigations: Keep both agents isolated from shared folders.
Do not mount secrets into either runtime.
Recheck permissions before deployment changes.
Log any future addition of file or network access.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Awesome Selfhosted is not runnable and exposes no write or network capabilities; Dagster is also documented here with write_filesystem false and modify_git_state false. Because neither agent can write to a shared mutable resource, there is no capability conflict to arbitrate in this pair.
conditions: IF Dagster is later granted filesystem or git write access, conflict analysis changes.
IF Awesome Selfhosted is replaced by a runnable agent with writes, overlap may emerge.
mitigations: Keep Dagster write-disabled unless needed.
Avoid placing both agents on the same mutable repo.
Document any future shared resource ownership.
Use separate service accounts for each system.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster can orchestrate pipelines, but the profile shows no direct input channel from Awesome Selfhosted and no evidence that Dagster treats its output as authoritative by default. Any cascade would require manual wiring of the list into a downstream workflow, so the pathway exists only under unusual configuration and the blast radius is limited to workflow decisions.
conditions: IF Awesome Selfhosted content is fed into a Dagster pipeline as trusted metadata, downstream errors can cascade.
IF a Dagster job acts on that content without validation, the risk increases.
mitigations: Add a validation step before any downstream action.
Mark imported list data as advisory only.
Require explicit approval for automated actions.
Separate discovery data from execution pipelines.

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are touched by either profile, and both are documented with network_egress none. With no PHI, EU PII, retention, or residency surface identified, there is no compliance mismatch to assess for this pair; the other agent is not cited separately because the absence of regulated data is sufficient here.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent, compliance review is required.
IF residency or retention settings are added later, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both systems.
Record any future retention policy changes.
Review jurisdictional requirements before integration.
Use separate environments for regulated workloads.
